messages:
anika: Heads-up — Olive9b (int4) canary started throwing OOMs under steady load. Reproducer attached in CI logs, failing around prefix-heavy chat workloads.

jamie: Can you paste the tail of the logs? stack/trace?

anika: ```
2026-03-20T14:02:21Z ERROR inference: alloc failed: out of memory
... runtime: alloc failed while prefetching KV pages
KV cache size jumped ~3x when max_new_tokens=512 + prefetch=256
```

infra-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy failed for olive9b-int4-v1 on pool-gpu-a (instance id i-0abc123). Auto-rollback triggered.

sasha: Not surprising — hypothesis: memory fragmentation + aggressive prefetch + default max_new_tokens=512. Int4 reduces model bytes but KV and transient buffers still spike.

liam: Quick perf snapshot from local repro (qps soak 60s):
- before (defaults): 420 qps, p95 latency 78ms, OOMs ~2/hour
- tuned (prefetch=64, max_new_tokens=128): 385 qps, p95 85ms, OOMs 0
Tradeoff: ~8-9% throughput loss but stability restored.

anika: Proposed immediate mitigations: reduce prefetch to 64, set default max_new_tokens=128 for olive9b int4, enable slot_compaction on warmstart, and add soft-kv-trim at 0.8 threshold.

jamie: Do we have a config snippet to push to canary?

sasha: Use this minimal override for canary route:```
model: olive9b-int4-v1
serve_preset:
  prefetch_pages: 64
  max_new_tokens_default: 128
  warmstart_compact: true
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.8
  batch: {max_batch_tokens: 4096, min_batch_size: 2}
```
Note: keep `max_batch_tokens` to avoid tiny microbatches under chat loads.

anika: Added a short warmup routine to our canary script so slot_compact runs after the first 30 warm requests. That reduces fragmentation from cold-to-warm transitions.

liam: Ran a quick benchmark with the override + 60s warmup:
- steady qps 370, p95 90ms, memory headroom +14% on average, OOMs 0
Also verified no quality regression on our eval set (BLEU-ish parity on synth QA).

bench-bot: Canary bench link: https://bench.redwood/olive9b/1752467890 . Summary: latency +5ms p95, throughput -11%, mem-95th down 18%.

jamie: Sounds reasonable as a temporary default. Longer-term we should investigate:
- kernel scheduling to reduce transient alloc spikes
- smarter prefetch heuristics (workload-aware prefetch)
- per-route max_new_tokens overrides in Console UI

sasha: Agreed. Action items: 1) push canary override (anika), 2) monitor OOMs/latency for 24h (jamie), 3) schedule kernel investigation with infra (liam).

anika: Pushed canary config and created ticket INF-5421 for the kernel/alloc follow-up.

infra-bot: Ticket created: INF-5421 — "olive9b int4 transient allocs / kernel sched / prefetch heuristics". Assigned liam and eng-infra.

jamie: I'll add a dashboard card for OOM-rate and mem-95 for olive9b routes and set an alert at 3 OOMs / 1h.

anika: Thanks — will keep this canary live for 24h and post results. :thumbsup:

sasha: If stable at 24h, roll the override into staging defaults and add a dev-notes snippet explaining the throughput/stability tradeoff.

liam: One more note: for very short-chat workloads we can raise `max_batch_tokens` to regain some throughput without increasing prefetch. We tested 6144 -> recovers ~4% qps. We'll include that as a follow-up experiment.

anika: All good. Closing the thread for now, will reopen if OOMs reappear. :white_check_mark:
